links.comparator_used: Performance on all samples (no uncertainty screening) versus samples below the 95th-percentile epistemic uncertainty threshold; flagged samples were set aside for review
links.outcome: Macro-F1 and robustness to temporal drift; capture of prediction errors by flagged samples
links.effect: Samples below the threshold had consistently higher macro-F1 and performance virtually invariant to temporal drift across all training-test time pairs; flagged samples captured most prediction errors (no numeric values in the abstract)
links.quote: Results across all training-test time pairs show that samples below this threshold exhibit consistently higher macro-F1 and render performance virtually invariant to temporal drift, while the flagged samples captured most prediction errors.

links.comparator_used: Running the model on all samples without an uncertainty-based out-of-distribution flag
links.outcome: Macro-F1 and error capture when potential OOD samples were flagged using Monte Carlo Dropout epistemic uncertainty
links.effect: Unflagged (in-distribution) samples had consistently higher macro-F1 and were virtually invariant to temporal drift; flagged potential OOD samples captured most prediction errors (no numeric values in the abstract)
links.quote: Results across all training-test time pairs show that samples below this threshold exhibit consistently higher macro-F1 and render performance virtually invariant to temporal drift, while the flagged samples captured most prediction errors.

design_hint: uncertainty thresholding for out-of-distribution detection and clinician review triage
